message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical Tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge a security deposit, but it cannot exceed **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit or **three months’ rent** for a furnished unit.
• The deposit must be held in a **separate, interest‑bearing account** (unless the landlord is a Texas bank).
• Within **30 days** after you move out, the landlord must return the deposit (or provide a written itemized list of deductions) | • Get a written receipt for the deposit.
• Take photos of the unit before moving in and after moving out. | | **Habitability** | • Landlords must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition**. This includes functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, and structural integrity.
• The landlord must repair any major defects within a reasonable time after notice. | • Document problems (photos, written notice).
• If repairs are not made, you may withhold rent or pursue a “repair‑and‑deduct” remedy (but only for certain repairs). | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are **reasonable** (usually not more than 5% of the monthly rent). | • Keep records of all payments. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a lease with **30 days’ written notice** (for month‑to‑month agreements).
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord must give you a **written notice of non‑renewal** at least **30 days** before the lease ends. | • Provide written notice in person or via certified mail. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlords cannot enter the unit without **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) unless there is an emergency. | • Ask for a written notice of entry. | | **Discrimination** | • Texas law (and federal Fair Housing Act) prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income. | • Report any discriminatory actions to the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlords must follow the **Texas Property Code** eviction procedure: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for non‑payment, 30‑day notice for lease violation).
• If you do not comply, the landlord must file an eviction lawsuit (unlawful detainer). | • Respond promptly to notices.
• If you believe the eviction is unlawful, you can file a counter‑claim or seek a stay of eviction. | | **Repair‑and‑Deduct** | • Under Texas Property Code §92.006, you may withhold rent or deduct repair costs if the landlord fails to fix a major defect. | • Only for repairs that are **necessary for habitability** and that cost less than the rent. | | **Right to Privacy** | • Landlords must respect your privacy; they cannot conduct searches without a warrant or a court order, except in emergencies. | • Keep a copy of any entry logs. | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify who pays utilities. If the landlord pays, they must maintain the utility service. | • Verify utility responsibilities in the lease. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • The lease may restrict subletting; if it does, you must obtain written permission. | • If you need to sublet, ask for written approval. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlords must keep common areas (hallways, stairwells, laundry rooms) safe and clean. | • Report any hazards. | | **Landlord’s Right to Inspect** | • Landlords can inspect the unit for maintenance or safety reasons, but must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours). | • Keep a log of inspections. | ### Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Look for clauses on rent, deposits, maintenance, entry, and termination. 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written notices, and receipts. 3. **Know the Notice Periods** – 30 days for most lease terminations, 24 hours for entry. 4. **Keep Copies of All Correspondence** – Emails, texts, letters. 5. **Know Your Local Resources** – * Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) – tenant‑rights information. * Texas Commission on Human Rights – discrimination complaints. * Local tenant‑rights groups or legal aid clinics. ### When to Seek Legal Help - **Unlawful Eviction**: If you receive an eviction notice that seems unjustified. - **Discrimination**: If you suspect the landlord is treating you unfairly. - **Major Habitability Issues**: If the landlord refuses to repair serious problems. - **Security Deposit Disputes**: If the landlord wrongfully withholds your deposit. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is intended for general educational purposes and does not constitute legal advice. Laws can change, and specific circumstances may alter how the law applies. If you have a particular issue, consider contacting a licensed attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.
